frozen_original.title: Hegseth, Lutnick Stock Trades Before Tariff Market Crash
frozen_original.synopsis: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth sold between $100,000 and $550,000 in stocks on March 24, 2025 — exactly one week before Trump's April 2 'Liberation Day' tariff announcement caused a major market crash. Hegseth's sales included Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, Walmart, Lowe's, and about 20 other companies, almost all of which saw prices plummet post-announcement. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reported 20 stock sales estimated at $401.4 million between March and October 2025, and separately sold $151.5 million in BGC Group shares and $127 million in Newmark Group shares. USA Today analysis found top Trump officials' stock sales statistically clustered before tariff news, including sales by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Deputy DHS Secretary Troy Edgar. Ethics experts said the trades did not 'appear' to use non-public information but that officials should have divested before taking office. No investigation was opened.

primary.decision_rationale: The frozen record combines Hegseth’s March 24 disclosure with Lutnick’s later divestitures. OGE and SEC records support two discrete events with different dates and purposes; neither source establishes insider trading or a shared tariff-related episode.

children.description_short: Pete Hegseth’s filed financial report lists multiple stock sales dated March 24, 2025.
children.description_medium: ProPublica’s reproduction of Hegseth’s federal transaction report lists multiple stock sales dated March 24, 2025, including Walmart, Microsoft and Apple. The disclosure records reported value ranges; it does not establish a trading motive, nonpublic information or a link to tariff policy. This card separates Hegseth’s transactions from Lutnick’s later ethics-agreement divestiture.
children.description_long: Pete Hegseth’s public financial disclosure, reproduced by ProPublica and available as an Office of Government Ethics transaction report, lists multiple stock sales dated March 24, 2025. The report names Walmart, Thermo Fisher Scientific, PepsiCo, Microsoft, Lowe’s, Apple, Alphabet, T-Mobile, Amazon and other securities; each transaction is shown with a reported value range rather than an exact proceeds figure. This card isolates those disclosed transactions from Howard Lutnick’s later sales under an ethics agreement. The disclosure establishes that transactions were reported on that date, but it does not establish why each sale was made, whether tariff information played any role or whether the trades produced a particular gain or loss. It provides no basis to treat the sales as insider trading or to attribute them to a specific policy announcement. No finding of misconduct is supplied. The entry records the disclosure and its timing, while leaving motive and any connection to government information unresolved.

children.title: Lutnick’s Newmark Divestiture Followed His Ethics Agreement
children.description_short: Howard Lutnick began selling Newmark holdings under an ethics agreement in May 2025 and completed the divestiture in October.
children.description_medium: Newmark’s SEC filing says Howard Lutnick agreed on May 16, 2025, to sell company shares as part of divestment required under his ethics agreement. It reports initial closings in May and completion on October 6. The filing identifies ethics compliance as the purpose; it does not establish a connection to tariff information.
children.description_long: Newmark Group’s annual filing to the SEC reports that Howard Lutnick agreed on May 16, 2025, to sell 10,969,533 Newmark Class A shares he beneficially owned. The filing says the first closing, for 10,839,674 shares held by Lutnick, his spouse and trusts, occurred May 19; a further 129,859 retirement-account shares were tied to later regulatory closing conditions. It states these transactions were pursuant to Lutnick’s agreement to divest company interests to comply with U.S. government ethics rules connected to his appointment as Commerce secretary. Newmark then reported that he completed his divestiture on October 6 and no longer had voting or dispositive power over the company’s securities. This is a separate ethics-agreement divestiture, distinct from Pete Hegseth’s March 24 transaction report. The filing does not connect Lutnick’s sales to tariff information or suggest they were pre-announcement trades. The record therefore describes a disclosed compliance process and does not treat the divestitures as evidence of opportunistic trading.

source_fact_map.fact: Lutnick agreed on May 16, 2025, to sell 10,969,533 Newmark Class A shares.
source_fact_map.quote: On May 16, 2025, Mr. Howard Lutnick, the U.S. Secretary of Commerce and the Company’s former Executive Chairman and former Chairman of the Board, agreed to sell to the Company 10,969,533 shares of Newmark Class A common stock beneficially owned by him
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: On May 16, 2025, Mr. Howard Lutnick, the U.S. Secretary of Commerce and the Company’s former Executive Chairman and former Chairman of the Board, agreed to sell to the Company 10,969,533 shares of Newmark Class A common stock beneficially owned by him, including (i) 7,989,936 shares held directly by Mr. Lutnick, (ii) 2,843,781 shares held in Mr. Lutnick’s personal asset trust, (iii) 3,384 shares held by the Mr. Howard Lutnick Family Trust, (iv) 2,573 shares held by Mr. Lutnick’s spouse, and (v) 129,859 shares originating from retirement accounts, including certain shares held by Mr. Lutnick’s spouse. The closing of the sale of the 10,839,674 shares held by him, his spouse, and the trusts occurred on May 19, 2025, and the closing of the sale of 129,859 shares held in retirement accounts will occur immediately after the closing of the sale of the voting shares of CFGM by Mr. Lutnick, which are pending subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approvals. These transactions are pursuant to Mr. Howard Lutnick’s agreement to divest his interests in the Company to comply with U.S. government ethics rules in connection with his appointment as the U.S. Secretary of Commerce. On October 6, 2025, Mr. Howard Lutnick, the U.S. Secretary of Commerce and the Company’s former Executive Chairman and former Chairman of the Company’s Board, completed his previously announced divestiture of his holdings in the Company in connection with his appointment as the U.S. Secretary of Commerce. Mr. Howard Lutnick no longer has any voting or dispositive power over any of the securities of the Company.

frozen_original.title: Trump Declares 'National Emergency' to Bypass Regulations Across Multiple Sectors
frozen_original.synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order declaring a general national emergency across multiple policy areas including energy, immigration, and economic policy, using the declaration as a legal lever to bypass environmental regulations, safety requirements, and administrative procedure requirements that would otherwise require notice-and-comment rulemaking. The sweeping use of emergency declaration authority to bypass normal regulatory processes was challenged as an abuse of the National Emergencies Act, which requires genuine crises rather than policy preferences to justify emergency declarations. Legal scholars warned the omnibus emergency declaration approach could permanently transform governance by allowing any administration to bypass regular legal process indefinitely.

primary.split_reason: The frozen description combines two distinct presidential actions. The supplied proposal identifies separate January 20, 2025 White House documents, and fresh primary-source retrieval confirms each declaration independently. The omnibus claim and regulatory-bypass characterization are not retained.

children.title: Trump Declares a National Emergency at the Southern Border
children.description_short: A January 20, 2025 proclamation declared a southern-border emergency and directed military support for border operations.
children.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a proclamation declaring a national emergency at the U.S. southern border. The text invokes emergency and military authorities and directs the Defense Department to support Homeland Security with personnel, logistics, and additional barriers. It records the administration’s stated actions, not proof that each measure was implemented or that the proclamation’s factual assertions were accurate.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a proclamation declaring a national emergency at the U.S. southern border. The text invokes sections of the National Emergencies Act and makes military authorities available, including provisions under Title 10, sections 12302 and 2808. It directs the Department of Defense to support the Department of Homeland Security through personnel, detention space, transportation, logistics, and additional physical barriers. The proclamation states these measures are intended to help the federal government obtain operational control of the border. This entry records the declaration and its stated directives; the text alone does not show which measures were implemented or their effects. It also does not establish the accuracy of the proclamation’s claims about conditions at the border. The original held item incorrectly presented this as one omnibus emergency covering immigration, energy, and economic policy and asserted that it bypassed environmental, safety, and notice-and-comment requirements. The national energy emergency appears in a separate presidential action issued on the same date, and the supplied documents do not support the broader bypass claim.

source_fact_map.fact: Trump’s proclamation declares a national emergency at the southern border and invokes statutory emergency authority.
source_fact_map.quote: hereby declare that a national emergency exists at the southern border of the United States
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including sections 201 and 301 of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.), hereby declare that a national emergency exists at the southern border of the United States, and that section 12302 of title 10, United States Code, is invoked and made available, according to its terms, to the Secretaries of the military departments concerned, subject to the direction of the Secretary of Defense.

source_fact_map.fact: The proclamation directs Defense to support Homeland Security’s border operations with military resources and logistics.
source_fact_map.quote: shall order as many units or members of the Armed Forces, including the Ready Reserve and the National Guard
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Section 1. Deployment of Personnel and Resources. frozen_original.title: DOGE Gains Unauthorized Access to Federal Court Electronic Filing Systems
frozen_original.synopsis: In March 2025, reports emerged — confirmed by congressional testimony of court IT administrators — that personnel associated with Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency had obtained unauthorized access to PACER and CM/ECF, the federal court electronic filing and case management systems that contain sensitive legal filings, sealed documents, grand jury materials, attorney-client communications, and protected personal information of litigants. The systems are administered by the Administrative Office of the United States Courts under the supervision of the federal judiciary — a constitutionally independent branch — and are explicitly not subject to executive branch direction. Intelligence officials described the access as a potential national security breach given the sensitivity of sealed filings involving counterterrorism, organized crime, and witness protection. Federal court administrators filed emergency notifications with the Chief Justice's office. The episode raised fears the administration was mining court filings to identify and target litigation adversaries.

primary.title: DOGE Gains Unauthorized Access to Federal Court Electronic Filing Systems
primary.description_short: The supplied claim that DOGE personnel accessed PACER or CM/ECF is not substantiated by the reviewed sources.

source_provenance.access_status: testimony fetched; it describes CM/ECF and PACER but does not report the alleged DOGE access
source_provenance.accessed_excerpt: The Judiciary’s case management/electronic case files (CM/ECF) system and its portal, the Public Access to Court Electronic Records (PACER) system.

blockers: The frozen synopsis alleges that DOGE personnel obtained unauthorized access to the federal judiciary’s PACER and CM/ECF systems and says court IT administrators confirmed it in congressional testimony. No such testimony or source URL is supplied, and the targeted searches did not locate credible reporting or testimony substantiating this event.

Search results surfaced separate DOGE access disputes involving executive-branch agency records and a report that DOGE briefly limited Treasury’s access to PACER. Those are different systems or access events and do not substantiate unauthorized access to federal judiciary filing systems.

The two successfully fetched official judiciary documents establish the scope of PACER/CM/ECF but do not report the alleged incident. The claim’s core event, affected accounts, authorization status, and date therefore remain unresolved.
